CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: Set 99% settle times for rk3399-gru The DVS rails were originally all set to a 200 us settle time because: * They were calculated based on 90% rise. * They were all given different amounts of slack to make the numbers look pleasing to the eye (200 is really pretty, isn't it?) Let's change this to be based on 99% rise. It's also silly to arbitrarily give each value a different amount of slack. Now we'll actually include the raw numbers here based on calculations. It's presumed that the fact that we're waiting for 99% rise is enough to give a little bit of slack anyway. These numbers are also the worse case rise time. If we really need extra slack, we should add a number that's a percentage of the real value, not something to just make a nice round number. BUG=chrome-os-partner:58432 TEST=Stability test Change-Id: Ie59a9d5f9fc3283cfb7c583054479798ccc32ae8 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/396528 Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: config: arm64: panic on hardlockup detect We've had this set to panic-on-hardlockup for a long time for rk3288/arm32. Let's do that for rk3399/arm64 too. This helps for debugging and collecting crash information, since otherwise a hardlockup is not guaranteed to trigger the panic handlers (which we recently instrumented for rk3399 to use ARM debug infrastructure to dump info about recently-retired instruction addresses). BUG=chromium:654931, chrome-os-partner:58229 TEST=`echo HARDLOCKUP > /sys/kernel/debug/provoke-crash/DIRECT`; see panic, instead of indefinite hang Change-Id: I45f407539d59ff6404e47ec774078874b4c63153 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/396396 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org>
